html:
SMTO-MEM-0042 — Knowledge is busy processing other work

GUID: bfaf8b30-4cec-500d-bc31-febe6ad155c5
Slug: knowledge-worker-busy
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • Knowledge's helpers were all busy, for example reading large documents. Your request waited too long and was stopped. Other work that was already running isn't stopped by this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Knowledge and look at your documents. Wait until none show Reading document, Preparing search or Updating search index. These documents are using the helper your request needed.
  2. Repeat your search. If a document shows Indexing failed, select Retry failed jobs instead of uploading it again. Once a helper is free, the same work can run normally, and retrying avoids a second copy.
  3. Avoid uploading many large documents at the same moment you need to search; add them in smaller groups. Large uploads keep the helpers busy for a long time.
  4. If it happens often, ask the person who manages SMTO to review the time and CPU limits under Administrator resource limits on the Document settings tab in Knowledge. More time or capacity lets requests wait their turn instead of stopping.

What success looks like

  • Your search returns results, or the document moves to Ready to search.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting how many documents were processing. Don't cancel or delete documents that are still processing just to make room.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Knowledge processing worker or the shared CPU thread budget stayed occupied by other indexing or search work past the request's deadline (worker queue or CPU budget deadline exceeded).

What this means

  • All eligible indexing capacity is occupied. Existing indexing jobs may still be progressing. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported worker_busy. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • A worker accepts the request after capacity becomes available.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Check document job states on the Knowledge page (or GET /api/agent/rag/jobs) and wait for extracting/embedding/indexing jobs to finish, then retry the search or use Retry failed jobs. If this recurs, an administrator can raise Maximum search worker time, Maximum ingestion time or the CPU thread budget under Administrator resource limits (Knowledge › Document settings).
  • Check indexing progress in Knowledge and wait for active jobs to finish before starting another operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • A worker accepts the request after capacity becomes available.

How to verify the fix

  • A worker accepts the request after capacity becomes available.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
